title: platform-systems-services-playbook-howtos-dashboards-runbooks-roadmap-retro-2026-q4
author: Ava Chen
body:
Overview

This document is the consolidated Platform Systems & Services playbook for Q4 2026. It contains: a concise systems overview, operational how-tos for common platform tasks, dashboards and alerting standards, runbooks for high-priority services, a short retrospective of major incidents in Q3-Q4 2026, and the platform roadmap for the next two quarters. The goal is to be a single operational reference for oncall, SREs, platform engineers, and cross-functional partners.

Scope and audience

- Scope: platform control plane services (platform-api, routing, quota, telemetry pipeline, dashboards/grafana), CI/CD orchestration, core infra automation, and observability primitives used by Redwood product teams.
- Audience: oncall, platform engineers, infra SREs, product engineers integrating with platform services.

Owner & escalation

- Primary owner: eng-platform (platform-systems team)
- Oncall rotation: Platform Oncall (PagerDuty) - escalation policy: 15 min P1 -> primary oncall, 15 min if no ack -> secondary, 20 min -> staff engineer, 30 min -> Director of SRE.
- Slack channel: #platform-ops (monitored during business hours)

System architecture summary

- platform-api: Kubernetes deployment (namespace: platform), exposes REST control plane for routes, tiers and model routing. Service name: platform-api.
- telemetry-pipeline: Kafka -> fluvio -> ingestion consumers -> clickhouse (metrics) and s3 (raw traces).
- dashboards: Grafana (v9) backed by ClickHouse + Prometheus federation for short term metrics.
- alerting: Alertmanager (global) routes to PagerDuty with team mapping.
- CI/CD: ArgoCD for infra manifests, GitHub Actions for release artifacts.

Operational SLOs & targets

- platform-api: availability 99.95% monthly; p95 latency for control API < 200ms; error rate < 0.1% (5xx).
- telemetry pipeline: ingestion lag < 60s 99th percentile; consumer error-rate < 0.5%
- dashboards (Grafana): UI availability 99.9%
- Alert delivery: 99% of pageable alerts should result in a PagerDuty page within 30s.

Dashboards and alerts (standards)

Dashboard guidelines

1. Every new service must ship a dashboard with at least: SLIs (availability, request latency, error rate), capacity metrics (CPU/GPU mem %), and key business signals (requests/min, tokens/sec).
2. Dashboards must include a short description and owner contact.
3. Use templated panels and standardized time ranges (1m/5m/1h).

Alerting policy (high level)

- Alert severity: P1 (page + Slack), P2 (Slack + email), P3 (dashboard only).
- Alert types that must be P1: service down (>=2 replicas not ready), sustained 5xx > 1% for 3m, telemetry ingestion lag > 5m, core quota service throttling affecting >5% of requests.
- Runbook-linked alerts: every P1 alert must include a runbook link and pagerduty escalation mapping.

Common alerting rules (examples)

- platform_api_5xx_rate: expr = sum(rate(http_server_errors_total{job="platform-api"}[3m])) / sum(rate(http_server_requests_total{job="platform-api"}[3m])) > 0.01 for 3m
- telemetry_consumer_lag_seconds: max_over_time(kafka_consumer_lag_seconds{consumer="telemetry-consumer"}[5m]) > 300
- grafana_ui_down: up{job="grafana"} == 0 for 2m

How-tos (frequent procedures)

1) Check platform health (first response)

- Step 1: Open primary health dashboard: Grafana -> Platform -> Overview.
- Step 2: Verify platform-api availability and pods: kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=platform-api
- Step 3: Check recent error spikes: Prometheus query: rate(http_server_errors_total{job="platform-api"}[5m])
- Step 4: Check telemetry pipeline lag: telemetry -> consumer-lag panel and kafka-lag PromQL (see rules above).

2) Restart a failing platform-api pod (safe restart)

- kubectl -n platform rollout restart deployment/platform-api
- Confirm new pods in Ready state: kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=platform-api -w
- If restart fails or crash-loop: collect logs: kubectl -n platform logs <pod> --previous; escalate to secondary oncall if crash loops > 5 restarts in 10m.

3) Promote Grafana dashboard changes (owner-reviewed)

- Create dashboard json, validate panels in staging Grafana, add owner/description, open PR in infra-dashboards repo, request review from observability team, merge -> Argo sync.

Runbooks (P1 examples)

Runbook: platform-api high 5xx rate

- Symptoms: sustained 5xx rate > 1% for 3m; users report control-plane failures.
- Impact: control plane operations (routing updates, rollouts) may fail; customer-facing inference unaffected unless routing changes are required.
- Owner: platform-systems oncall
- Steps:
  1. Acknowledge PagerDuty and post to #platform-ops with incident tag.
  2. Check replicas and pod logs: kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=platform-api; kubectl -n platform logs <pod> -c platform-api --since=10m
  3. Check downstream store (etcd) connectivity: curl -sS http://etcd.internal:2379/health
  4. If transient (spike < 10m) watch for recovery. If persistent, scale up replicas: kubectl -n platform scale deployment/platform-api --replicas=<current+2>
  5. If errors indicate DB errors, failover read-only replica and escalate to infra-db team.
  6. After mitigation, add timeline and notes to the incident postmortem template and mark for triage.

Runbook: telemetry ingestion lag high

- Symptoms: consumer lag > 5 minutes, late dashboards, missing traces.
- Owner: observability team
- Steps:
  1. Check Kafka consumer group: kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group telemetry-consumer
  2. Restart consumer pod if stuck: kubectl -n observability rollout restart deployment/telemetry-consumer
  3. Check ClickHouse ingestion errors in logs and disk pressure in ClickHouse cluster.
  4. If backlog is large, enable consumer autoscale for 30m and apply temporary higher concurrency.

Post-incident retrospective (Q3-Q4 2026 highlights)

- Incident A (2026-07-14): Grafana outage caused by a bad alertmanager config that created metric-cardinality storm. Root cause: unbounded label expansion on a new instrumentation. Actions: added cardinality limits to metrics ingestion, alertmanager config validation, and CI check for high label cardinality.
- Incident B (2026-09-03): Telemetry ingestion lag due to Kafka broker disk pressure. Root cause: delayed compaction and retention misconfig. Actions: improved broker monitoring, reserved disks for Kafka, and autoscale for telemetry consumers.
- Lessons learned:
  - Validate metrics cardinality and add tests in the instrumentation PR checklist.
  - Runbook drills twice per quarter with synthetic alert firing.
  - Require every producible alert to have a runbook link before being promoted to P1.

Action items (owners)

- Add cardinality CI checks to instrumentation pipeline (owner: observability, ETA: 2026-11-01).
- Implement runbook drill calendar and automate synthetic alerts (owner: SRE, ETA: 2026-12-01).
- Increase platform-api horizontal autoscaling ceiling (owner: platform-systems, ETA: 2026-11-15).

Roadmap (next two quarters)

Priority themes Q4 2026 - Q1 2027:

1) Unified alerting & routing
- Migrate Alertmanager instances to a central, team-aware routing plane with per-tenant silencing and faster failover. Goal: reduce duplicate pages by 40%.

2) Dashboard migration to Grafana v10 + standardized templates
- Convert all platform dashboards to templated dashboards with shared variables and reuseable panels. Goal: 95% dashboard coverage by Q1 2027.

3) Runbook automation & testing
- Build CI that validates runbook links for alerts and runs synthetic alerting tests on merge. Goal: every new alert has a tested runbook.

4) Observability for Private deployments
- Provide a lightweight monitoring agent + dashboards for Private customers and integrate with Redwood Console.

5) Cost and capacity improvements
- Implement smarter retention and ingest sampling for metrics to reduce ClickHouse spend by 15% without losing SLO coverage.

Appendix: quick references

- PagerDuty: Redwood Platform schedule -> https://pagerduty.com/redwood/platform
- Grafana overview dashboard -> Grafana -> Platform -> Overview
- ArgoCD sync: argocd.redwood.internal -> platform manifests repo: git.redwood.internal/infra/platform-manifests
- Incident postmortem template: /confluence/eng-platform/incident-postmortem-template

Contact and feedback

For corrections or updates to this playbook, open a PR in the infra-docs repo or contact the platform-systems team via Slack (lead: @ava.chen).
